newsitem.title: UK: FedEx MD11 insured for about $100 mln-market.
newsitem.headline: FedEx MD11 insured for about $100 mln-market.

text.p: An MD11 cargo aircraft which crashed overnight at Newark International Airport had an insured value of around $100 million, London insurance market sources told Reuters.
The aircraft, which was operated by Federal Express, was insured on the international aviation insurance market.
Lloyd's of London Archer Group was lead underwriter on the risk, London sources said. Nobody at Archer, which was acquired last year by Chartwell Re, was immediately available to comment.
A spokesman for Aon Group Limited, London, a part of Aon Corp, said it was insurance broker for FedEx, but could give no further details.
London insurers said this would probably be the biggest aviation hull loss so far this year.
Recent figures from UK based Airclaims put total hull losses of Western-built jets for the first six months of 1997 at $168.6 million.
The wide-body aircraft, which was arriving from Anchorage, Alaska, crash landed, flipped over and burst into flames, airport officials said.

The five flight crew crawled to safety through a cockpit window after the cargo jet overturned on landing at 1:35 a.m. EDT (0535 GMT) about 200 yards (metres) from a terminal, a spokesman for the New York/New Jersey Port Authority said.

"It was a very hard landing," Port Authority spokesman Allen Morrison said. "The plane, on impact, flipped over and began to burn. All five crew members on board were able to crawl out the cockpit window.
At 4:15 a.m. EDT, Morrison said firefighters were still battling the burning wreckage with foam and the airport, one of the busiest in the U.S., was closed indefinitely.
"Pieces of the plane are scattered on the runway," Morrison added. CBS radio reported that the fuselage was missing both wings and the tail section.
They reported that an eye-witness had seen flames coming from the cargo plane before it landed.
